$comment: Names and ids only, never a secret. The crew addresses Airtable by NAME and
resolves each name to your base's ids at startup, so a duplicated base needs
only a new airtable.baseId. Change a name only if your base renames the field.

airtable.$comment: Table and column names are Title Case, matching the base exactly. Airtable resolves table names case-sensitively.

choices.$comment: Cell VALUES, not column names — left exactly as the base spells them today. The Development formula matches these literally. Parity Status is inconsistent between the token tables (Base Tokens: 'In Testing', Semantic Tokens: 'In testing') and still needs a decision.

figma.$note: Only tokens is required. One Figma file? set tokens, leave components blank. Components are read per-row from Airtable, so add component files only if you want them named here.

stack.$note: Set at /productive-crew:setup. Decides the component code AND the token output. Regenerates tools.md.

repo.$note: Branch names are yours. Defaults below. If your repo already uses develop/master or another flow, /productive-crew:setup detects it and maps the three tiers (work → preview → production) to your branches. If you rename these, also update the branch refs in .github/workflows/pages.yml.

tokenBuilder.$note: The build runs when tokens/tokens.json changes. The schedule is a safety net for when a change lands without triggering a run — not the primary trigger.

deploy.$note: enabled=false is NOT WIRED YET: no staging link, so no QA stage and no Staging Testing rows. provider decides WHO publishes the staging build — the crew only needs a URL it can verify, and it does not care who produced it.
deploy.$providerNote: github-pages = the bundled .github/workflows/pages.yml builds and publishes on push. command = you publish, with the commands below — use this for Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, surge, an internal host, or whenever GitHub Actions is unavailable to you. The contract for a command is exactly one thing: print the deployed URL as the LAST line of stdout. The Engineer captures that line, verifies it answers 200, and reports it.
